data.body:
Root cause identified with a class-level reproduction, 2026-11-12 PST: this is bald-diagnostic-cricket (cded-334b-a742-4082), fixed by a9300a8b2f2 "Send rebar diagnostics to the process stderr". The observed commit 1bfa37ca141 does NOT contain a9300a8b2f2 (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` says no); current main does.
- Cause: install_stderr_handler built StreamHandler(sys.stderr), freezing whatever stderr object was current at install; the install is idempotent, so once that capture stream closed, the next rebar warning (here the "no resolvable identity (author_id)" authorship warning) became "--- Logging error --- Traceback" written into the test's captured stderr, failing its "no Traceback" assertion. The live-tracker symlink only decided whether that warning fired, which is why the sighting tracked it. The test itself writes its tickets to its own tmp store; it does not read the cwd tracker.
- Reproduction (pytest plugin that installs the handler under a since-closed stderr, then emits the identity warning inside the test): at 1bfa37ca141, 3 of 3 FAIL with the exact message from the report ("--- Logging error --- Traceback ... no resolvable identity (author_id) for this writer"); at current main 0fccb0f20aa, 3 of 3 PASS. A9300a8b2f2's handler writes to sys.__stderr__, so no rebar log record can reach a capsys stream at all.
- Also confirmed: with a fake (empty) .tickets-tracker symlink in the checkout, the test passes at both commits, so the symlink is not itself a factor.
Closing as duplicate of bald-diagnostic-cricket; no code change needed.
